key_insight: ADC-GNN improves few-shot graph fraud detection by combining diffusion-based feature augmentation, contrastive learning, and multi-hop spectral attention to combat sparse labels and oversmoothing.
engineering_relevance: The method is relevant for transaction-scale fraud systems because it targets low-label, imbalanced graphs where robust detection must work under strict data and compute constraints.
method: Diffusion-guided node-feature augmentation creates noise-perturbed views with a cosine schedule for contrastive stabilization.
Contrastive learning aligns representations across perturbations to reduce sensitivity to scarce supervision.
Multi-hop spectral attention highlights fraud-relevant relation and frequency cues that may be lost in standard message passing.
evidence_signal: The paper reports consistent gains under the 1% training setting on three public benchmarks, plus a private telecom transaction case study with about 60,000 records.
watch_item: Because the diffusion module augments features rather than topology, performance may depend on how well the perturbation schedule and spectral settings match each graph’s noise level and class imbalance.
paper_title: Beyond Sparse Supervision: Diffusion-Guided Learning for Few-Shot Graph Fraud Detection
